g.text: "description": "Per-case judge override. enabled: false skips goal-completion grading for this case; null clears the overrid
e and restores the suite setting."
"description": "The suite file's own `suite.id`, when THIS request is a suite-file sync.\n\nA CI-owned suite (see `EvalSuite
Detail.managedBy`) refuses configuration writes with `409` and `details.reason: \"CI_OWNED_SUITE_READ_ONLY\"`. Naming the suite's
own declared id is how the file writing itself is allowed through: the platform permits the write only when the id matches, so nam
ing any other id refuses exactly as loudly as naming none. Omit it for ordinary edits.\n\nPREFER THE `declaredSuiteId` QUERY PARAM
ETER on this route. This body field still works here, but these request bodies are strict on every Inspector that predates the CI-
owned lock, so a body field is a `400` against an older deployment while an unknown query parameter is simply ignored. The MCPJam
SDK and CLI send the query parameter."
"description": "Stable declared id for the case: the id it answers to in a suite file, an import or a CLI argument. Minted f
or you when omitted, and unique within the suite. Distinct from the `id` on the response, which is the case's platform row id."
"description": "REPLACES the case's test definition wholesale when provided."
"description": "The legacy per-case count, which the legacy resolver reads as a FLOOR (`max(legacyIterations, suite.minimumI
terations)`). Stored as `runs`. Vocabulary 1 spells this field `iterations`; under `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary: 2` that key is the e
xact configured count, so the floor answers to this name (legacy spelling `runs`). NOT the same field as `iterations`: the two are
never a both-spellings pair, and a PATCH that names neither leaves the stored floor exactly as it was."
"description": "Legacy spelling of `legacyIterations`. Send one spelling only."
"description": "The exact number of iterations this case runs under per-case grading, overriding the suite default (vocabula
ry 1 spells it `repetitions`). PER-CASE GRADING ONLY: on a suite decided by the suite-wide accuracy threshold this is a VALIDATION
_ERROR naming the criterion change that would make it readable, because that criterion takes the count from the case's own `legacy
Iterations` raised to the suite's `minimumIterations` and would never read this. A CREATE that names this but no `legacyIterations
` stores the floor at the same value; a CREATE that names neither stores a floor of 1. Capped at 10."
